Where it began

Lungi Ngidi was born in Durban on 29 March 1996 and grew up in Kloof. A scholarship took him to Highbury Preparatory School, and another to Hilton College. He played rugby there for three years before choosing cricket, and at Hilton he was coached by Neil Johnson, the former Zimbabwe all-rounder. After school he went to the University of Pretoria to study industrial sociology.

He played for Northerns in the 2015 Africa T20 Cup, and in 2016 Cricket South Africa named him the competition's player of the year.

The player

His international career began in style. On his T20 International debut, against Sri Lanka in January 2017, he was man of the match. A year later he joined the Test squad partway through the series against India, and on his debut on 13 January 2018 he took 6 for 39 in the second innings, 7 for 87 in the match, as South Africa won by 135 runs.

Between 2018 and 2025 he played 20 Tests and took 58 wickets at 23.38, with three five-wicket innings. His most important Test came in June 2025, when South Africa met Australia in their first World Test Championship final. After a wicketless first innings he took 3 for 38 in the second, and South Africa went on to win by five wickets.

What made him special

He had a gift for big occasions. In March 2020 he took his first five-wicket haul in one-day internationals, against Australia, and in the same game reached 50 one-day wickets in his 26th match, quicker than any South African before him. Cricket South Africa named him one of its five Cricketers of the Year in 2018, and in 2020 made him both its ODI and its T20I cricketer of the year.

Batting was another matter. His 97 Test runs came at 4.85, with a top score of 19. Yet he was not out 11 times in 31 innings, so he was harder to get rid of than the average suggests.

Around the world

Teams in many places wanted him. Chennai Super Kings bought him at the 2018 IPL auction and Delhi Capitals in 2022, and in 2023 he joined San Francisco Unicorns for the first season of Major League Cricket in the United States. At home he played for Tshwane Spartans in the Mzansi Super League as well as for Northerns. In 2019 the ICC picked him as one of eight players to watch at that year's IPL.

And finally

Taking six wickets in an innings on Test debut is a fine thing. Being part of the side that wins a world title is even better. Ngidi managed both, seven years apart, which is a neat pair of bookends for any bowler's shelf.
